data.one_liner: Type‑safe Dart API for accessing and managing the Windows Registry
data.what_it_does: Provides high‑level, strongly typed methods to read, write, delete, and monitor registry keys and values, with support for transactions and change notifications.
use_when: Windows desktop applications that need to read or modify registry settings
Installers or setup utilities that configure system or application settings
Tools that monitor registry changes for dynamic configuration
avoid_when: Applications that prefer cross‑platform configuration storage (e.g., JSON, SQLite)
strengths: Type‑safe, high‑level API built on win32
No need to write raw FFI code
weaknesses: Adds a dependency on win32 and ffi_leak_tracker

alternatives.name: win32
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides lower‑level Win32 API access, useful if you need more control than win32_registry offers
